events.fact: Slack OAuth apps are registered via the Slack API developer portal at https://api.slack.com/apps.
Slack apps use a v2 OAuth 2.0 flow with redirect endpoint https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize and token endpoint https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access.
Any developer can build, distribute, and install an app via unlisted public distribution (Activating Public Distribution in app settings) without Slack review.
Slack-side review and approval are only required if you choose to list your app in the official Slack Marketplace for commercial distribution.
Prerequisites for submitting to the Slack Marketplace include: app must be fully tested, publicly available, and installed on 10 or more active workspaces (used in the past 28 days).
Marketplace review timelines are up to 10 business days for preliminary review and up to 10 weeks for functional review of new submissions.

Slack apps not listed in the Marketplace may trigger warning screens or be blocked if the workspace has 'Require apps from Slack Marketplace' or 'Require approved apps' enabled in App Management Settings, which admins can disable or bypass by configuring custom OAuth credentials.

Slack rate limits are applied per API method per workspace per app and are categorized into tiers ranging from Tier 1 (1+ request/min) to Tier 4 (100+ requests/min), with custom tiers for posting messages.

Slack scopes are divided into bot scopes (prefixed with bot token) and user scopes (user_scope), covering chat, channels, files, search, and admin functions. Sensitive or restricted scopes require justification during Marketplace review.
